comment: She's incredibly two-faced and if you make one tiny mistake, she'll never forget it and hold a grudge against you for the rest of the semester. She purposely waited until after course evals to not respond to emails and give terrible feedback. I spoke to classmates and the criticism she gives my work compared to theirs is way harsher for no reason

If youre actually looking to improve your writing skills, Monika gives great advice and feedback though she is a tough grader. Every class is basically a long discussion about an assignment or the homework. Theres almost no way to calculate your grade as theres no outlined grading criteria, but if you work hard and PARTICIPATE shell reward you.

Monika is an incredible person and cares very much about her students. However, she is an extremely tough grader and nobody will get an A on the first paper. This FYS requires a massive amount of reading (usually 100 pages per week). I wouldn't take her again because of this, but I learned so much about refugees and I improved my writing skills.

Monika is really sweet and personable, however, I like her more as a person than a professor. She doesn't give A's on papers and grades based on improvement, which I found confusing. There's a ton of homework. She'll also go off on tangents only loosely related to what we're talking abt. I learned a lot abt the refugee crisis and loved what we read

Monika was a very kind teacher and I enjoyed the layout of how she would teach each classes. I will say there was a fair amount of reading in this class so beware of that but other than that it wasn't a difficult FYS.

Dr. Siebert is great and always willing to meet outside class if you need help. The subject was interesting but the class would get boring somedays. The workload was fine but sometimes I felt like I had more homework than my peers taking another FYS class. I would recommend taking her if you want to improve your writing skills.
Dr. Siebert is great, but the amount of reading can feel excessive at times. If you're looking to improve your writing though, taking her is well worth it.

I really enjoyed her class and found that she made it easier to get to know people in the class. She is fairly picky about the essays so you really have to follow a basic structure. I found getting an essay to where she wanted it the hardest part. Overall, interesting subject though and wanted to go to class every week.

Dr. Siebert is so caring! She always makes sure to give super clear feedback on essays because she genuinely cares that all of her students become better writers. At the end of the semester, she also takes into account how much you improve as a writer which is nice. Participate in the class and listen to her feedback on essays and you will do well.

Monika is one of the sweetest professors at Richmond. She is super caring and always keeps the interests of her students in mind. She is super intelligent and gives amazing feedback on papers. She definitely improved my writing in her Refugee FYS. The class gets a little boring and there is a lot of reading but I didn't do any of it lol.
Dr. Siebert is by far one of the most caring and invested professors at UR. Her courses are among the best and most educational I've taken during my time here.

I wanted to enjoy this class more than I actually did. The material was interesting and I learned a lot, but the professor had a tendency to be scattered. Many times I felt like we never covered what we were supposed to, and that the direction of the class was lacking. She also had a heavy focus on films, which was odd for an English course.

Dr. Siebert is a harsh grader (especially on the first paper), but her feedback is very thorough and she is always willing to work with you to improve. She's also an awesome person to talk to outside of class and strives to make all of her students' voices heard on campus. The class is participation heavy (socratic seminar style).

I took her Refugees FYS. We read 4 books + some articles, and wrote 3 papers. For each day of class she would ask us to read 70-170 pages and write a short paragraph. The class was mostly discussion of the text, but the discussion often felt one-sided/ biased and therefore uninteresting. Her grading was confusing, and my final grade was a surprise.

Awesome professor! She's incredibly smart and dedicated to making her students learn. She makes you read a lot and there are quizzes, but if you put in the work then it all pays off. Tough grader, especially with essays, but if you meet with her and put the effort in she'll give you all the resources to succeed.

Dr. Siebert is exceedingly intelligent, dedicated to her work, and really cares about her students. If you have trouble meeting a deadline, she is very accommodating. Such a nice woman, but she also makes you think hard about the subject matter. I learned a lot from her class and would definitely take her again.

I took America in the World the World in America FYS and while she is a tough grader her feedback is easily understood and she will work with you to revise papers until they're what she expects. Class participation is crucial, which isn't difficult since she leads discussions very well. Good mix of books and movies studied. Take her class!
